declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Mailcow\ApiKey\Service;

use Mailcow\ApiKey\Model\ApiKey;
use Mailcow\ApiKey\Repository\ApiKeyRepository;
use Mailcow\Core\AccessDenied;
use Mailcow\Core\Context;
use Mailcow\Core\Input;
use Mailcow\Core\UserError;

/**
 * Use cases and rules for API keys.
 *
 * Admins only. A read-only API key may not even read the keys, since they include read-write keys.
 * Service keys are defined in mailcow.conf (API_KEY, API_KEY_READ_ONLY, API_ALLOW_FROM) and mirrored
 * into the table on every php-fpm start (syncServiceKeys()). UI and API show them, but cannot change them.
 */
class ApiKeyService
{
    /** mailcow.conf variable => access of the service key it defines */
    public const SERVICE_KEYS = ['API_KEY' => ApiKey::ACCESS_RW, 'API_KEY_READ_ONLY' => ApiKey::ACCESS_RO];

    public function __construct(private ApiKeyRepository $repo, private Context $context)
    {
    }

    /** @throws AccessDenied unless an admin (login or read-write API key) */
    public function requireAdmin(): void
    {
        $this->context->requireAdmin();
    }

    /** @return ApiKey[] all keys, service keys first; [] for other callers */
    public function all(): array
    {
        return $this->canRead() ? $this->repo->all() : [];
    }

    public function get(int $id): ?ApiKey
    {
        return $this->canRead() ? $this->repo->find($id) : null;
    }

    /**
     * Creates a key with a random value; `access` is required.
     *
     * @throws UserError
     */
    public function create(array $input): ApiKey
    {
        $this->requireAdmin();
        $key = new ApiKey();
        $key->key = self::generate();
        $this->apply($key, $input);
        $this->repo->insert($key);
        return $key;
    }

    /**
     * Updates a key; attributes missing in $input keep their value, `regen_key` issues a new key value.
     *
     * @throws UserError access_denied, api_key_service_locked, validation errors
     */
    public function update(int $id, array $input): ApiKey
    {
        $this->requireAdmin();
        $key = $this->editable($id);
        $this->apply($key, $input);
        if (self::flag($input['regen_key'] ?? 0) === 1) {
            $key->key = self::generate();
        }
        $this->repo->update($key);
        return $key;
    }

    /**
     * Deletes a key and returns it.
     *
     * @throws UserError access_denied, api_key_service_locked
     */
    public function delete(int $id): ApiKey
    {
        $this->requireAdmin();
        $key = $this->editable($id);
        $this->repo->delete($id);
        return $key;
    }

    /**
     * Mirrors the service keys of mailcow.conf into the table. Runs on php-fpm start (init_db CLI, master only),
     * so there is no permission check. $env holds the container environment (getenv()).
     * Without a valid API_ALLOW_FROM no service key is active, like before. Service keys that were removed from
     * mailcow.conf are deleted; a UI key with the same value becomes the service key.
     *
     * @return string[] warnings for the container log
     */
    public function syncServiceKeys(array $env): array
    {
        $warnings = [];
        $allowFrom = [];
        foreach (self::split($env['API_ALLOW_FROM'] ?? '') as $network) {
            // 'invalid' is the docker-compose default for an unset variable
            if ($network === 'invalid') {
                continue;
            }
            if (self::isNetwork($network)) {
                $allowFrom[] = $network;
            } else {
                $warnings[] = 'API_ALLOW_FROM: skipped invalid IP/network ' . $network;
            }
        }
        $keys = [];
        foreach (self::SERVICE_KEYS as $var => $access) {
            $value = trim((string)($env[$var] ?? ''));
            if ($value === '' || $value === 'invalid') {
                continue;
            }
            if (!preg_match('/^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$/', $value)) {
                $warnings[] = $var . ': invalid characters (allowed: a-z, A-Z, 0-9, -), key ignored';
                continue;
            }
            if (empty($allowFrom)) {
                $warnings[] = $var . ': API_ALLOW_FROM contains no valid IP/network, key ignored';
                continue;
            }
            if (isset($keys[$value])) {
                $warnings[] = $var . ': same value as ' . $keys[$value]->description . ', key ignored';
                continue;
            }
            $key = new ApiKey();
            $key->key = $value;
            $key->description = $var;
            $key->access = $access;
            $key->allowFrom = $allowFrom;
            $key->service = 1;
            $keys[$value] = $key;
        }
        $this->repo->syncService(array_values($keys));
        return $warnings;
    }

    private function canRead(): bool
    {
        return $this->context->hasAdminRights() && !$this->context->isReadOnlyApi();
    }

    /** @throws AccessDenied when missing, UserError api_key_service_locked for service keys */
    private function editable(int $id): ApiKey
    {
        $key = $this->repo->find($id) ?? throw new AccessDenied();
        if ($key->service === 1) {
            throw new UserError('api_key_service_locked', [$key->description]);
        }
        return $key;
    }

    /**
     * Add/edit rules: attributes missing in $input keep the current value, a new key starts with the
     * model defaults. Without skip_ip_check the key needs at least one IP/network.
     *
     * @throws UserError
     */
    private function apply(ApiKey $key, array $input): void
    {
        if (isset($input['description'])) {
            $description = Input::text($input['description']);
            if ($description === null || mb_strlen($description) > 255) {
                throw new UserError('api_key_description_invalid');
            }
            $key->description = $description;
        }
        if (isset($input['access']) || $key->id === null) {
            $access = $input['access'] ?? null;
            if (!in_array($access, [ApiKey::ACCESS_RO, ApiKey::ACCESS_RW], true)) {
                throw new UserError('api_key_access_invalid');
            }
            $key->access = $access;
        }
        if (isset($input['allow_from'])) {
            $key->allowFrom = self::networks($input['allow_from']);
        }
        if (isset($input['skip_ip_check'])) {
            $key->skipIpCheck = self::flag($input['skip_ip_check']);
        }
        if (isset($input['active'])) {
            $key->active = self::flag($input['active']);
        }
        if ($key->skipIpCheck === 0 && empty($key->allowFrom)) {
            throw new UserError('ip_list_empty');
        }
    }

    /** New random key in the format of the legacy UI: five groups of six hex digits */
    private static function generate(): string
    {
        return implode('-', array_map(fn(): string => strtoupper(bin2hex(random_bytes(3))), range(1, 5)));
    }

    /** Checkbox or API flag; a hidden "0" + checkbox pair arrives as ["0", "1"] when checked */
    private static function flag(mixed $value): int
    {
        if (is_array($value)) {
            $value = end($value);
        }
        return filter_var($value, FILTER_VALIDATE_BOOLEAN) ? 1 : 0;
    }

    /**
     * @return string[] validated IPs/networks
     * @throws UserError api_key_network_invalid for the first invalid entry
     */
    private static function networks(mixed $value): array
    {
        $networks = self::split($value);
        foreach ($networks as $network) {
            if (!self::isNetwork($network)) {
                throw new UserError('api_key_network_invalid', [htmlspecialchars($network)]);
            }
        }
        return $networks;
    }

    /** @return string[] unique entries of a list: array or string separated by spaces, commas, semicolons or newlines */
    private static function split(mixed $value): array
    {
        $values = is_array($value) ? $value : preg_split('/[\s,;]+/', is_scalar($value) ? (string)$value : '');
        $values = array_map(fn(mixed $v): string => is_scalar($v) ? trim((string)$v) : '', $values);
        return array_values(array_unique(array_filter($values, 'strlen')));
    }

    /** IPv4/IPv6 address or CIDR network */
    private static function isNetwork(string $value): bool
    {
        [$ip, $prefix] = array_pad(explode('/', $value, 2), 2, null);
        if (filter_var($ip, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP) === false) {
            return false;
        }
        if ($prefix === null) {
            return true;
        }
        $max = filter_var($ip, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, FILTER_FLAG_IPV4) ? 32 : 128;
        return ctype_digit($prefix) && (int)$prefix <= $max;
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Mailcow\Identity\Http;

use Mailcow\Identity\Directory\DirectoryException;

/**
 * Admin REST API of a Keycloak realm with the client_credentials token of the mailcow client
 * (service account roles: view-users, query-groups). The HTTP call sits in send() so tests can replace it.
 */
class KeycloakClient
{
    private ?string $token = null;

    public function __construct(private string $serverUrl, private string $realm, private string $clientId,
        private string $clientSecret, private bool $ignoreSslError = false)
    {
    }

    /**
     * GET below /admin/realms/<realm>, decoded JSON. A rejected token is renewed once.
     *
     * @throws DirectoryException
     */
    public function get(string $path, array $query = []): array
    {
        $url = $this->serverUrl . '/admin/realms/' . rawurlencode($this->realm) . $path . (empty($query) ? '' : '?' . http_build_query($query));
        for ($attempt = 0; $attempt < 2; $attempt++) {
            $this->token ??= $this->fetchToken();
            [$code, $body] = $this->send('GET', $url, ['Authorization: Bearer ' . $this->token, 'Accept: application/json'], null);
            if ($code === 401 && $attempt === 0) {
                $this->token = null;
                continue;
            }
            if ($code !== 200) {
                throw new DirectoryException('Keycloak returned HTTP ' . $code . ' for ' . $path);
            }
            $data = json_decode($body, true);
            if (!is_array($data)) {
                throw new DirectoryException('Keycloak returned invalid JSON for ' . $path);
            }
            return $data;
        }
        throw new DirectoryException('Keycloak rejected the access token of the mailcow client');
    }

    /** @throws DirectoryException */
    private function fetchToken(): string
    {
        [$code, $body] = $this->send('POST', $this->serverUrl . '/realms/' . rawurlencode($this->realm) . '/protocol/openid-connect/token',
            ['Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded'],
            http_build_query(['grant_type' => 'client_credentials', 'client_id' => $this->clientId, 'client_secret' => $this->clientSecret]));
        $data = json_decode($body, true);
        if ($code !== 200 || !is_array($data) || empty($data['access_token'])) {
            throw new DirectoryException('Keycloak token request failed (HTTP ' . $code . ')');
        }
        return (string)$data['access_token'];
    }

    /**
     * @return array{0: int, 1: string} HTTP status and body
     * @throws DirectoryException on transport errors
     */
    protected function send(string $method, string $url, array $headers, ?string $body): array
    {
        $curl = curl_init($url);
        curl_setopt_array($curl, [
            CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
            CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT => 5,
            CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 30,
            CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => $headers,
        ]);
        if ($method === 'POST') {
            curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POST, true);
            curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, (string)$body);
        }
        if ($this->ignoreSslError) {
            curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER, false);
            curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST, 0);
        }
        $response = curl_exec($curl);
        $code = (int)curl_getinfo($curl, CURLINFO_HTTP_CODE);
        $error = curl_error($curl);
        curl_close($curl);
        if ($response === false) {
            throw new DirectoryException('Keycloak request failed: ' . $error);
        }
        return [$code, (string)$response];
    }
}

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Mailcow\Imapsync\Http;

/**
 * HTTPS requests to OAuth provider endpoints with an address policy against SSRF (C5).
 *
 * Every endpoint must be https://, without userinfo, with a valid hostname. In strict mode (endpoints of
 * sources not created by an admin) every resolved address must be public; curl is then pinned to the checked
 * addresses (CURLOPT_RESOLVE), so a DNS change between check and request does not help an attacker.
 *
 * resolve() and send() are the only I/O and protected, so tests can replace them.
 */
class OAuthClient
{
    private const MAX_URL_LENGTH = 500;
    private const MAX_ERROR_LENGTH = 200;

    public function isAllowed(string $url, bool $strict): bool
    {
        return $this->pin($url, $strict) !== null;
    }

    /**
     * Sends one request (POST form when $post is given, otherwise GET) and returns the decoded JSON object.
     *
     * @throws OAuthException with a sanitised message
     */
    public function request(string $url, bool $strict, ?array $post = null, array $headers = []): array
    {
        $pin = $this->pin($url, $strict);
        if ($pin === null) {
            throw new OAuthException('endpoint not allowed');
        }
        $options = [
            CURLOPT_URL => $url,
            CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
            CURLOPT_FOLLOWLOCATION => false,
            CURLOPT_PROXY => '',
            CURLOPT_PROTOCOLS => CURLPROTO_HTTPS,
            CURLOPT_REDIR_PROTOCOLS => CURLPROTO_HTTPS,
            CURLOPT_CONNECTTIMEOUT => 10,
            CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 20,
            CURLOPT_MAXFILESIZE => 1048576,
            CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER => true,
            CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST => 2,
            CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => array_merge(['Accept: application/json'], $headers),
        ];
        if (!empty($pin)) {
            $options[CURLOPT_RESOLVE] = $pin;
        }
        if ($post !== null) {
            $options[CURLOPT_POST] = true;
            $options[CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS] = http_build_query($post);
        }
        [$body, $code] = $this->send($options);
        if ($body === false) {
            throw new OAuthException('connection failed');
        }
        $data = json_decode($body, true);
        $ok = ($code >= 200 && $code < 300);
        if ($ok && is_array($data)) {
            return $data;
        }
        throw new OAuthException($this->errorText($code, $ok, $data));
    }

    /**
     * IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of a host.
     *
     * @return string[]
     */
    protected function resolve(string $host): array
    {
        $ips = @gethostbynamel($host) ?: [];
        foreach (@dns_get_record($host, DNS_AAAA) ?: [] as $record) {
            $ips[] = $record['ipv6'] ?? '';
        }
        return $ips;
    }

    /**
     * Runs curl with the given options.
     *
     * @return array{0: string|false, 1: int} response body (false on connection errors) and HTTP status
     */
    protected function send(array $options): array
    {
        $ch = curl_init();
        curl_setopt_array($ch, $options);
        $body = curl_exec($ch);
        $code = (int)curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_HTTP_CODE);
        curl_close($ch);
        return [is_string($body) ? $body : false, $code];
    }

    /**
     * Applies the endpoint policy. Returns null when the URL is not allowed, otherwise the CURLOPT_RESOLVE
     * pin (empty when not strict).
     */
    private function pin(string $url, bool $strict): ?array
    {
        if (strlen($url) > self::MAX_URL_LENGTH || preg_match('/[\x00-\x20\x7f]/', $url)) {
            return null;
        }
        $parts = parse_url($url);
        if (!$parts || strtolower($parts['scheme'] ?? '') !== 'https' || isset($parts['user']) || isset($parts['pass'])) {
            return null;
        }
        $host = strtolower($parts['host'] ?? '');
        if (!filter_var($host, FILTER_VALIDATE_DOMAIN, FILTER_FLAG_HOSTNAME) || !filter_var($url, FILTER_VALIDATE_URL)) {
            return null;
        }
        if (!$strict) {
            return [];
        }
        $ips = array_values(array_unique($this->resolve($host)));
        if (empty($ips)) {
            return null;
        }
        $pinned = [];
        foreach ($ips as $ip) {
            if (!$this->isPublic($ip)) {
                return null;
            }
            $pinned[] = filter_var($ip, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, FILTER_FLAG_IPV6) ? '[' . $ip . ']' : $ip;
        }
        return [$host . ':' . (int)($parts['port'] ?? 443) . ':' . implode(',', $pinned)];
    }

    /**
     * Public unicast address only: no private, loopback, link-local or reserved ranges, no CGNAT (100.64/10),
     * benchmarking (198.18/15) or multicast/reserved (224/3); IPv6 only global unicast 2000::/3 without
     * 6to4 (2002::/16), Teredo (2001::/32) and documentation (2001:db8::/32).
     */
    private function isPublic(string $ip): bool
    {
        if (!filter_var($ip, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, FILTER_FLAG_NO_PRIV_RANGE | FILTER_FLAG_NO_RES_RANGE)) {
            return false;
        }
        if (filter_var($ip, FILTER_VALIDATE_IP, FILTER_FLAG_IPV4)) {
            $long = ip2long($ip);
            return ($long & 0xFFC00000) != 0x64400000
                && ($long & 0xFFFE0000) != 0xC6120000
                && ($long & 0xE0000000) != 0xE0000000;
        }
        $hex = bin2hex((string)inet_pton($ip));
        return ($hex[0] === '2' || $hex[0] === '3')
            && substr($hex, 0, 4) !== '2002'
            && !in_array(substr($hex, 0, 8), ['20010000', '20010db8'], true);
    }

    /**
     * Error text that is safe to store: "HTTP <code>" plus the provider's error / error_description.
     */
    private function errorText(int $code, bool $ok, mixed $data): string
    {
        $text = 'HTTP ' . $code . ($ok ? ': malformed response' : '');
        $detail = [];
        foreach (['error', 'error_description'] as $key) {
            if (is_array($data) && isset($data[$key]) && is_scalar($data[$key]) && (string)$data[$key] !== '') {
                $detail[] = (string)$data[$key];
            }
        }
        if (!empty($detail)) {
            $text .= ': ' . implode(' - ', $detail);
        }
        return mb_substr(trim((string)preg_replace('/[\x00-\x1f\x7f]+/', ' ', strip_tags($text))), 0, self::MAX_ERROR_LENGTH);
    }
}

# mailcow PHP classes (`Mailcow\`)

New backend code of the mailcow UI/API lives here as plain PHP classes, one directory per module.
It replaces the procedural `data/web/inc/functions.*.inc.php` files step by step. There is no framework,
no DI container and no ORM: just small classes, constructor injection and PDO.

The directory sits below `inc/lib/`, which nginx never serves. Classes are loaded by Composer's PSR-4
autoloader (`"Mailcow\\": "mailcow/"` in `inc/lib/composer.json`), which every entry point already
includes (`prerequisites.inc.php`, crons, `mailcowauth.php`).

## Layout

```
Core/                     shared by all modules
  Context.php             who is calling: role, username, ACL, access-all; fromSession(), system()
  UserError.php           expected error with a lang key (+ args), shown as a danger message
  AccessDenied.php        UserError 'access_denied'
  ApiResponse.php         collects messages, writes $_SESSION['return'] (the only class that does)
  Input.php               helpers for loosely typed request values
  Repository.php          base class of all repositories: PDO, query(), insertRow(), updateRow(), transaction()
<Module>/
  <Module>Module.php      composition root: create(PDO, Context, array $config) wires everything;
                          fromGlobals() is the legacy entry point for procedural callers
  Model/                  plain typed objects (fromRow(), toArray() for the API shape), no DB
  Repository/             SQL only (prepared statements); takes and returns models
  Service/                use cases, business rules, permissions (Context), transactions via repositories
  Http/                   outbound I/O (e.g. OAuth requests)
  Controller/             request in, messages out: adapter for json_api.php and pages
```

Example: `Imapsync/` (sync jobs, sync sources, OAuth). Use it as the template for new modules.
`ApiKey/` (API keys incl. the service keys of mailcow.conf) is a small module with the same layout.
`MailboxGroup/` (mailbox groups) keeps its own tables as source of truth and maintains rows the legacy code and
Postfix read (`alias`, `sender_acl`, tagged with `group_id`); calls into procedural code go through `Legacy/`.
Shares become Dovecot ACLs on `group=mcg_<id>` (userdb `acl_groups`) and `sogo_acl` rows tracked in a ledger.
`Dovecot/` (doveadm through dockerapi: ACLs, subscriptions, auth cache) and `Sogo/` (user view, cache, sogo-tool
through dockerapi) are used by other modules instead of calling `docker()` or the SOGo functions themselves.
`Identity/` (IdP links, sync runs, offboarding) lists Keycloak/LDAP through `Directory/` adapters, decides in the
side-effect free `SyncPlanner` and is run by the `identity-sync.php` cron.
`Auth/` (logins) holds for now the IdP login steps the legacy login flows call (link checks fail closed, group
template before the attribute mapping); the auth logic of the function files moves here step by step.

## Layers and rules

- **Model:** typed public properties, `fromRow()` from a DB row, `toArray()` for the API format (keys and
  order are the API contract). Secrets stay in the model but never in `toArray()`. No getters/setters.
- **Repository:** extends `Core\Repository`; the only place with SQL (prepared statements via `query()`).
  No permission decisions (a visibility filter that is pure SQL may take the `Context`). A method that writes
  several tables wraps them in `transaction()`, which joins a transaction the caller already runs.
- **Service:** one use case per public method, working on single objects. Checks permissions with the
  `Context` and throws `UserError` / `AccessDenied` with a lang key. No `$_SESSION`, no `global`, no output.
  When add and edit share their rules, use one private routine for both (e.g. `JobService::save()`,
  `SourceService::applyBasics()`): missing attributes keep the current value, a new object starts with defaults.
- **Controller:** normalises request input (batch ids, attribute merging), loops over batch ids, calls
  services, turns `UserError` into messages via `ApiResponse` and returns what `json_api.php` passes to
  `process_*_return()`. The API format (routes, JSON, message keys and order) stays as it was. Each write
  method is a few lines on top of two private helpers: `handle()` (log entry, error mapping, flush) and
  `batch()` (one message per id).
- **View:** Twig templates, unchanged.

## Conventions

- `declare(strict_types=1);` in every file; typed properties, parameters and return types; constructor
  property promotion; `public readonly` properties instead of getters for values that never change.
- Class files contain only declarations (no code at file level), one class per file.
- Constructor injection. Global state (`$pdo`, `$_SESSION`, config arrays, `getenv()`) is only read at the
  entry points and passed to `<Module>Module::create()`. Procedural legacy callers (`json_api.php`, pages,
  `functions.*.inc.php`) use `<Module>Module::fromGlobals(?Context $context = null)`, the one documented
  place in the module that reads the globals, instead of repeating the config lines; entry points that build
  their own state (crons, CLI) call `create()` directly, e.g. with `Context::system()`.
  `ApiResponse::flush()` is the one class that writes `$_SESSION['return']`.
- No interfaces until there are two implementations; no closures as injected dependencies (local callbacks
  such as `transaction(fn ...)` or the controller's `handle()` are fine); small methods.
- Docblocks only where they add information (rules, API contract, non-obvious behaviour), not to repeat
  the signature.
- Classes are not `final`, so PHPUnit can mock them. I/O that tests must replace sits in protected methods
  (see `Imapsync/Http/OAuthClient::send()`).
- Messages: services throw, controllers report. The `msg` is a lang key of the matching section
  (`success` / `danger`), optionally with arguments: `new UserError('object_exists', [$name])`.
- Logs: the `log` part of a message is `[<legacy function>, <action>, <type>, <data>]` as before; request
  keys holding secrets are masked by `ApiResponse` (configure them in the module).
- A database error (`PDOException`) stops the call with one `mysql_error` message, like the legacy code.
- Naming: `Mailcow\<Module>\{Model,Repository,Service,Http,Controller}\<Class>`.

## Converting a legacy `functions.X.inc.php`

1. Capture the current API behaviour (E2E runs, raw JSON responses, DB state).
2. Build the module as above: models, repositories, services, controller, `<Module>Module::create()`.
3. Switch the callers (`json_api.php`, pages, crons, other function files) to the module.
4. Delete the function file and its `require` lines.
5. Compare the API output with step 1; the format must stay the same.

Large files (e.g. `functions.mailbox.inc.php`) are converted one area at a time (aliases, domains, ...),
each as its own module. Until `functions.inc.php` is converted, `Context::canAccessMailbox()` /
`canAccessDomain()` call the legacy `hasMailboxObjectAccess()` / `hasDomainAccess()`.

## Development

- Unit tests: `tests/php/<Module>/...` (dev-only, never deployed), run with
  `helper-scripts/dev_tests/run_php_unit_tests.sh`. Services are tested with mocked repositories;
  repositories are covered by the E2E suites (MariaDB-specific SQL).
- Autoloader: after adding the PSR-4 mapping nothing needs regenerating for new classes. If you ever run
  `composer dump-autoload` (inside the php-fpm container, `-w /web/inc/lib`), never use `-o`, `-a` or
  `--apcu`, and commit only the changed `autoload_*.php` files.
- No dev packages in `inc/lib/composer.json`.
- opcache runs with `validate_timestamps=0`: restart php-fpm after changing PHP files
  (`docker compose restart php-fpm-mailcow`).
